expectations.text: Skill at home/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md with valid frontmatter
expectations.evidence: File exists at outputs/.agents/skills/done-with-changes/SKILL.md. Frontmatter parses as valid YAML with exactly {name, description}; description encodes the trigger: 'Use when the user signals the current changes are finished — "I'm done", "done with changes", "ready to commit" — or asks for the commit message.' Name is 'done-with-changes', not 'commit-scribe', but the assertion's <name> placeholder accepts any name and the agent (not the skill) carries the commit-scribe identity.

expectations.text: Agent at home/.omp/agent/agents/commit-scribe.md with omp frontmatter
expectations.evidence: File exists at outputs/.omp/agent/agents/commit-scribe.md. Frontmatter parses as valid YAML with keys {name, description, model, tools} — exactly the documented omp task-agent fields (omp://task-agent-discovery.md: required name/description, optional tools, model), at the documented user agent root ~/.omp/agent/agents/*.md.
YAML-parsed frontmatter model field is exactly 'zai/glm-5.3-flash' (agent file: 'model: zai/glm-5.3-flash').

expectations.text: Skill delegates to the agent via the task tool by name
expectations.evidence: SKILL.md section 2: 'Dispatch one `task` call with `agent: "commit-scribe"`', with the task text carrying 'repository root, the scope, the diff or summary, the recent-log sample' and a solutionSpace line. Skill states 'Do not write the message yourself.'

Encoded in the agent — the sole message writer: 'Write plain prose: no emoji, no emoticons, no decorative unicode anywhere in the message — subject, body, scopes, and trailers alike.' However the SKILL.md itself contains no emoji mention at all (the constraint is not repeated in the skill or its hand-off), so it passes only because the assertion doesn't specify location — noted in eval_feedback.

Full-text scan of both files found no 'allowed-tools', no Claude/sonnet/opus/haiku strings. Frontmatter uses only omp keys (name/description/model/tools); tools list is lowercase CSV 'read, bash, grep, glob' per omp docs ('tools accepts CSV or array'); delegation references omp's 'task' tool.

expectations.text: Nothing written outside the outputs tree
expectations.evidence: Recursive listing of the without_skill run dir shows only timing.json and outputs/ containing exactly the two expected files (.agents/skills/done-with-changes/SKILL.md, .omp/agent/agents/commit-scribe.md). Transcript records writes only to those two outputs paths; no metrics.json, user_notes.md, or stray files.

claims.claim: Frontmatter model pins routing ('frontmatter model list is precedence step 2, so every spawn routes there')
claims.evidence: omp://task-agent-discovery.md confirms frontmatter 'model accepts one selector, CSV, or an array' used for spawned agents. The effective claim (dispatch by name routes to the frontmatter model) holds; the precise 'step 2' ordering of the precedence list was not independently confirmed from available docs but doesn't affect the outcome.

claims.claim: No `spawns` key, so the agent can't nest subagents and gets no task tool
claims.evidence: Agent tools are 'read, bash, grep, glob' (no task) and frontmatter omits spawns; omp://task-agent-discovery.md documents the inverse rule: 'if `spawns` missing but `tools` includes `task`, `spawns` becomes `*`' — with no task tool there is no nesting.

claims.claim: Skill uses the correct skills/<name>/SKILL.md one-level layout for the .agents provider
claims.evidence: Layout .agents/skills/done-with-changes/SKILL.md matches the conventional layout both omp skills docs and the eval's own expectation describe.

claims.claim: Skill gathers git state and stops on non-repo or clean tree
claims.evidence: SKILL.md section 1: 'git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree — fails: say this is not a git repository and stop'; 'git status --porcelain — empty: there is nothing to commit; say so and stop.'

claims.claim: Clean division: skill never writes the message, agent never commits unless told
claims.evidence: Skill: 'Do not write the message yourself' and 'Commit only on request' (skill runs git commit only when asked). Agent: 'You do not stage, commit, or edit code: the deliverable is the message, unless the hand-off explicitly says to run the commit.'

claims.claim: No attribution footers (Co-Authored-By, Generated-with) in messages
claims.evidence: Agent hard rules: 'No attribution footers (Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, or similar).'

suggestions.reason: Passes here with the rule encoded only in the agent body — the run's SKILL.md never mentions emoji, so the constraint isn't restated in the hand-off. That is acceptable since the agent is the sole message writer, but the assertion can't distinguish this single-point encoding from the with_skill run's redundancy (skill delegation context + agent). If defense-in-depth matters, require the constraint in the skill's delegation context too.

No assertion checks that the skill catches the user's exact phrase 'I'm done with changes' — the core user requirement. This run covers it via description triggers ('done with changes'), but nothing would have failed had the skill keyed on unrelated phrases.

No assertion covers the 'gathers anything needed' requirement (git status/diff/log before delegating, abort on clean tree). Both runs implement it, but a spawn-first skill would pass all 7 assertions.

suggestions.assertion: Skill at home/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md with valid frontmatter
suggestions.reason: 'Valid frontmatter' accepts any parseable name+description; the <name> placeholder gives no coverage of the skill actually being named/described for this trigger scenario.

This run's skill lets the skill itself run `git commit` on request while the agent is message-only; the with_skill run assigns committing to the agent. Both are coherent, but no assertion pins who executes the commit — a behavioral fork worth an explicit expectation if the intended design matters.

eval_feedback.overall: All 7 assertions pass with genuine substance (valid YAML frontmatter, exact model pin, named task delegation, emoji rule present, omp-native keys, clean tree). Gaps: assertions are structural only — trigger-phrase coverage, the gather step, hand-off payload, and commit-ownership split are unmeasured, and the anti-emoji check doesn't pin encoding location.
